identification.title: Only a God Like You
identification.notes: Written by Tommy Walker alone; CCLI 3185395, published by Integrity Music (Capitol CMG Publishing administers). Recorded live at Christian Assembly in Los Angeles for the 2000 album Never Gonna Stop (Integrity, Hosanna! Music, Word), where it is the second track. The list's guess of Phillips, Craig and Dean is wrong; the song is Walker's own. The exact release date differs between sources (year 2000 either way). Reviewed as the song, not as any one recording.

claims.structuralNotes: A verse, a chorus, and a long extended section, returning to a chorus tag. The verse renounces human praise and worldly kingdoms in favour of serving the crucified Lord. The chorus declares that only this God is worthy of praise, hope and faith. The extended section moves to third person and lists titles of God and Christ - Maker, Father, Savior, Redeemer, Restorer - and recounts the incarnation, healing of the blind and the lost, the crown of thorns, and victory over sin and death. The voice is a first-person vow of allegiance; the long section is what Christ has done.

claims.claim: The singer renounces human praise and earthly kingdoms to serve the crucified Lord.
claims.subject: Allegiance to Christ

claims.claim: Only this God is worthy of praise, hope and faith; none is like him.
claims.subject: The uniqueness of God

claims.claim: God is Maker, Father, Savior, Redeemer and Restorer.
claims.subject: Titles and work of God

claims.claim: Christ took on human nature, humbling himself.
claims.subject: The incarnation

claims.claim: Christ restores the blind and the lost.
claims.subject: Christ's saving mercy

claims.claim: Christ wore the crown of thorns and won victory over sin and death.
claims.subject: Cross and victory

strengths.title: The uniqueness of God declared
strengths.explanation: The chorus puts hope and faith in this God alone, in the manner of the Song of Moses and Isaiah. It is a clear confession of monotheistic worship, not merely a mood.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Who is like you among the gods, O LORD - the question the chorus answers.

strengths.title: The incarnation and the cross sung together
strengths.explanation: The extended section names the Son's humbling, the crown of thorns and the defeat of sin and death. It teaches who Christ is and what he did, in order.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Christ taking human form and humbling himself to death - the arc the section follows.

strengths.title: Victory over sin and death named
strengths.explanation: The song ends its recital on Christ's conquest of sin and death, grounding the vow of allegiance in an achieved work.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Through death he destroyed the one who has the power of death, freeing those held in fear.

strengths.title: Allegiance to God alone
strengths.explanation: The verse sets the singer's service against human praise and worldly kingdoms, which is the first-commandment shape of true worship.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Worship the Lord your God and serve him only.

doctrinesAffirmed: God as Maker, Father and Redeemer
theological.assessment: Nothing to correct. The song is a confession that no other god or ruler deserves the singer's praise, and its long section grounds that vow in the incarnation, the cross and Christ's victory. Trinity is only implied by the Father and Christ both being named, and the Spirit and the church are not reached. No independent assessment of the song's teaching was found.

strengths.title: A simple chorus
strengths.explanation: The chorus is short and direct and easy to learn, even if the rest is heavy.

strengths.title: A song of allegiance
strengths.explanation: It suits a service about Christ's lordship or a call to worship him alone.

communal.vocalRangeNote: No chart was read, so no key advice is firm. The long extended section is heavy for a room and better led by a cantor or spoken; the chorus is the congregational part.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The chorus repeats and a tag returns after the long recital, so the room keeps coming back to the central confession.
communal.assessment: The chorus is easy for a room; the extended section is long and wordy, which makes the song harder to sing together than to listen to. A leader can shorten it.

strengths.title: Titles that identify the God being praised
strengths.explanation: Maker, Father, Savior, Redeemer and Restorer, with the work of Christ recounted, leave no doubt who is meant.

strengths.title: Vow, confession, recital
strengths.explanation: Allegiance, then the claim, then the reason, so each section answers why the singer can say what he does.

clarity.assessment: Clear. The titles are biblical and the recital follows the gospel narrative, so little is open to a wrong reading.

synthesis.summary: A vow of allegiance that confesses no other god or ruler deserves the singer's praise, hope or faith, followed by a long recital of God's names and of Christ's work: the incarnation, mercy to the blind and the lost, the crown of thorns, and victory over sin and death. No false or misleading teaching was found. The long section is lyrically heavy for a congregation. No independent assessment of the song was found.

scriptureReferences.relevance: Who is like the LORD among the gods - the chorus's confession.
Christ's humbling, incarnation and obedience to death.
Christ giving sight to the blind man.
The lost sheep sought and found.
The crown of thorns placed on Jesus.
Christ destroying the power of death.
The LORD will not give his glory to another.
